title: Adaptive reconnect handshake with ordered chunk reassembly and function-call boundary safety
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Improve the streaming HTTP event protocol to support adaptive reconnects and deterministic reassembly of out-of-order or partially-received chunks while preserving function/tool-call atomicity and structured output integrity. This ticket designs and implements a lightweight handshake and sequence-vector approach so clients may resume with minimal duplication, avoid delivering partial functioncall payloads, and respect server-directed backpressure hints.
context: We currently rely on simple byte-offset resume tokens and client heuristics for reassembly. That approach leads to duplicated fragments, accidental splitting of function call payloads, and poor latency under bursty workloads. A more explicit minimal enrichments to the event stream will let us achieve: 1) idempotent replays with exact chunk deduplication, 2) ordered reassembly across multiplexed logical channels (assistant messages vs functioncall frames), and 3) server-provided backpressure guidance to clients to adapt poll/reconnect frequency under load.
technical_design:
Proposal summary:
- Add a small framed header per chunk: {stream_id, chunk_seq, chunk_kind, checksum, optional_resume_hint}. The header is JSONL meta preceding the payload for readability and hybrid compatibility.
- stream_id scopes an ordered sequence for a logical output lane (e.g., default-assistant, function-call, tools).
- chunk_seq is a monotonic integer per stream_id used by clients to reassemble and detect gaps.
- chunk_kind identifies payload types: 'text', 'json-struct', 'toolcall-start', 'toolcall-data', 'toolcall-end'.
- checksum (SHA1 truncated) provides cheap validation to avoid silent corruption.
- optional_resume_hint is an opaque short token the server may offer as a prefered resume anchor to optimize subsequent resumes.
- Reconnect handshake: client reconnects and submits last-seen {stream_id:chunk_seq} map. Server compares and responds with minimal diff: 'resume_from' per stream_id and a small list of chunk_seq to re-send if gaps exist.
- Function-call atomicity: server ensures that toolcall-start and toolcall-end map to contiguous chunk_seq ranges in a stream_id; on reconnect the server will either resend the full atomic range or instruct the client to replay only missing chunk_seq.
- Backpressure: server emits a flow-control meta-event that includes 'target_client_window' (ms) and 'suggested_backoff' factor. Clients must respect suggested_backoff for reconnect storm prevention.
- Backward compatibility: if a client cannot parse the JSONL header, server falls back to legacy behavior (byte-offset resume). The header is optional; presence enables the advanced flow.
Implementation notes:
- Implement header parser in runtime streaming layer (golang) and in Node/Python SDKs.
- Add middleware that maps model output lanes to stream_id and guarantees chunk_seq assignment under concurrency.
- Store minimal per-connection resume state (recent 256 chunk headers) for quick resume without persistent storage.
- Add unit tests for partial replay, duplicate suppression, and functioncall reassembly.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Server emits headers and assigns stream_id/chunk_seq for all streaming responses in a backward-compatible fashion.
2) Client SDKs (Node + Python) can reconnect providing a last-seen map and receive a resume plan that results in no duplicated functioncall payloads in 95% of simulated reconnects.
3) End-to-end tests demonstrating ordering guarantees across default-assistant and functioncall lanes under concurrent tool invocations.
4) System gracefully falls back to legacy byte-offset resume with older clients and files deprecation telemetry.
5) No regression in median streaming latency; 95th percentile latency impact < 5% in internal perf benchmarks.
6) Observability: new dashboard panels showing resume events, gap frequency per stream, and backpressure signals sent.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for chunk header encode/decode, checksum validation, header parse errors.
- Integration test: simulated network partitions with random chunk drops and reconnects, assert reassembled payloads equal original.
- Load test: 1000 concurrent streaming clients with intermittent reconnects to measure resume latency and backpressure effectiveness.
- SDK conformance tests for Node and Python: handshake + resume flows.
- Manual QA: trigger a function that returns a large toolcall JSON and ensure no partial JSON delivered to client after reconnect.
- Add fuzz tests to ensure corrupt header handling doesn't crash runtime.
implementation_plan:
1) Prototype header format and small server proof-of-concept. (2d)
2) Runtime change: chunk allocator/middleware that stamps headers and keeps recent window. (5d)
3) Node + Python SDK change: header aware reconnect handshake and reassembly logic. (4d)
4) Add observability hooks and dashboards. (2d)
5) E2E tests and canary rollout on staging, then gradual rollout to production 5% -> 25% -> 100%. (6d)
Milestones: proto -> runtime PR -> SDK PRs -> staging canary -> production ramp.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff and design notes posted. Ava and Liam agreed on JSONL meta approach over a binary proto to ease debugging and provide graceful degradation.
2026-03-11: Runtime prototype implemented for header stamping. Basic tests show reduced duplication on simple reconnect scenarios. PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8762.
2026-03-12: SDK contract drafted. Node SDK handshake design reviewed by Marisol. Agreed to expose a low-level resume map API and higher-level auto-reconnect helper.
2026-03-13: Design review feedback: prefer 16-bit chunk_seq to reduce header size; add server-side retention window metric. Updating spec and plan.
risks:
- Increased header overhead could marginally raise network bytes for very small responses. We'll mitigate via compact headers and optional emission for tiny chunks.
- Complexity in guaranteeing atomic functioncall ranges under aggressive preemption; to mitigate, middleware will reserve chunk_seq ranges when starting toolcall emission.
- Client adoption required for full benefits; legacy clients will still see best-effort behavior and we will monitor via telemetry.
